paragraphs.text: Rebind the composer's send and newline keys in DeepSeek Harness — Enter sends, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter breaks
the line by default.
# dsh-enter-combination
中文说明

Pick which key sends a message and which key breaks the line in the DeepSeek Harness composer.
Enter
sends and ⌘/Ctrl+Enter breaks the line out of the box; either one can be re-recorded.
## Settings
设置 → 发送按键 (one section of its own in the settings drawer).
| Row | Default | What the key does in the composer |

| 发送 | `Enter` | sends the draft to the AI |
| 换行 | `⌘Enter` on macOS, `Ctrl+Enter` elsewhere | move
s the caret to the next line, without sending |
Click a key button and press the combination you want: the next real key is recorded together with t

he
modifiers held at that moment, and the row shows it right away. `Esc` cancels, clicking the butto

n
again cancels too, and a chord the other row already owns is refused with a one-line hint instead

of
silently shadowing it.
## How it hooks the composer

Both chords are shipped internal wiring — the composer's own keymap turns Enter into a submit and
Sh
ift+Enter into a line break, and neither is exposed as a slot. So this plugin listens for `keydown`
on `document` in the capture phase, before the composer sees it, and then replays the shipped path:
- **send** → the session's public submit action (`conversation.input.for(scope).actions.submit()`),

the same transaction the Send button runs. Two guards: a held key does not queue a burst of sends,
a

nd a composer with no session behind it is left alone so its own Enter still works.
- **newline** →

re-dispatches a `Shift+Enter` keydown on the composer's contenteditable, which is
exactly the chord

the editor already treats as a line break. The replay is untrusted, so the
listener ignores it.

A composing IME keeps its Enter: while the input method is composing, both chords are left to the
co

sing IME keeps its Enter: while the input method is composing, both chords are left to the
composer.
## Storage
`localStorage['dsh-enter-combination']`, per browser profile. There is no host half to persist: only

this page's composer reads the mapping, and the mapping is two chords. The cost is that the same
pr
ofile opened on another machine starts from the defaults again.
## Install
Needs a DeepSeek Harness build that loads plugin bundles (`dsh.bundle` in `package.json`).
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That links the folder into the active profile (`link:` in the profile `package.json`) and adds the
b
undle to `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the profile tracks this source tree instead of a copy.

`client.js` is re-read on every page load, but the plugin itself only mounts when Harness boots:
res

tart Harness (quit and reopen the app) to see the section for the first time. Later edits to
`client
.js` only need a page refresh.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`test/self-check.mjs` loads `client.js` the way the module loader does, stubs the DOM, and asserts t

he
interception (defaults, the shift-enter replay, unrelated inputs, IME, held key, no session) and

the
recorder (recording a chord, cancelling with Esc, refusing the chord the other row owns, unusabl

e
storage falling back to the defaults).
## Limits

- The chords are matched on `event.code` plus the four modifier flags, so they follow the physical
k

ey rather than the layout's character: `⌘Enter` stays `⌘Enter` on a Dvorak layout, and two keys
that

produce the same character are still two different chords.
- Characters that come from the layout (

e.g. `⌘↩` vs `⌘Enter`) are the same chord; the row shows the
name of the code that was recorded.
- W

hile a row is recording, the next chord anywhere on the page goes to the recorder — not just keys
pr

essed inside the composer.
- The mapping is a browser-profile preference: it does not travel with th

e session, and another
browser/OS profile starts at the defaults.
